raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose
Resolves an open `TODO` in `hadacore_transform_kernel` regarding the removal of `matrix_transpose_m8_n8_b16_inplace` to decrease latency. 

The TODO suggested finding an alternative storage method to avoid the transpose overhead. However, empirical testing on an RTX 3070 Ti (sm_86) confirms that the kernel is heavily memory-bandwidth bound. Removing the warp shuffles produces incorrect mathematical output while yielding **zero end-to-end performance improvement**, as the instruction latency is completely hidden behind global memory stalls. 

This PR removes the obsolete TODO and updates the documentation to reflect that the current transpose implementation is optimal given the memory bounds.
## Test Plan
Ran the custom benchmarking script to compare end-to-end latency and throughput across various `hidden_dim` sizes in both `square` and `tokens` configurations:
```bash
python develop-eggs/cuda_kernels/bench_hadacore.py
```
Analyzed the speed-of-light (SOL) hardware utilization via Nsight Compute:
ncu --import develop-eggs/cuda_kernels/hadamard_kernel_profile.ncu-rep
## Test Result
Nsight Compute confirms the kernel is fully bottlenecked by VRAM bandwidth, achieving 88.07% DRAM Throughput compared to only 34.41% Compute Throughput:
((venv) ) [prakhar@acer vllm]$ ncu --import develop-eggs/cuda_kernels/hadamard_kernel_profile.ncu-rep 
[601694] python3.12@127.0.0.1

    Section: GPU Speed Of Light Throughput
    ----------------------- ----------- ------------
    Metric Name             Metric Unit Metric Value
    ----------------------- ----------- ------------
    DRAM Frequency                  Ghz         6.99
    SM Frequency                    Ghz         1.40
    Elapsed Cycles                cycle      952,570
    Memory Throughput                 %        88.07
    DRAM Throughput                   %        88.07
    Duration                         us       679.36
    L1/TEX Cache Throughput           %        35.59
    L2 Cache Throughput               %        36.25
    SM Active Cycles              cycle   937,916.63
    Compute (SM) Throughput           %        34.41
    ----------------------- ----------- ------------

    INF   This workload is utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance of this device.  
          To further improve performance, work will likely need to be shifted from the most utilized to another unit.   
          Start by analyzing DRAM in the Memory Workload Analysis section.                                              

    Section: GPU Speed Of Light Roofline Chart (Overview)
    INF   The ratio of peak float (FP32) to double (FP64) performance on this device is 64:1. The workload achieved 0%  
          of this device's FP32 peak performance and 0% of its FP64 peak performance. See the Profiling Guide
